_doc: Towns at the start year of one civilisation. Each entry: name, tile (a real tile id of the base map, found by placing lat/lon in the map's equal-area grid), lat, lon, and `sizes`, a list of dated snapshots {year, people, low, high, source, conf}. people is the point figure, low and high the range the literature gives; conf follows the map's letters (A checked against the cited source, B coordinate checked and size approximate, C from memory of a secondary compilation, D a weak guess). A size is an initial condition (cited, never tuned); the engine does not read it. Sizes of ancient and medieval towns differ by a factor of two or more between authors, which `low` and `high` show.

sizes.source: Chandler, Four Thousand Years of Urban Growth (1987); Modelski, World Cities: -3000 to 2000 (2003). The Eastern Han capital; the point figure is the high end.
Chandler, Four Thousand Years of Urban Growth (1987); Modelski, World Cities: -3000 to 2000 (2003). Western Han capital, past its peak by this date.
Modelski, World Cities: -3000 to 2000 (2003); far below its Warring States size
